title: Sociology, B.S. (College of the Liberal Arts)
notes: University Park. Sibling of the already-built Sociology B.A. (SOCBA-2026.json), reusing soc_catalog.json's already-fixed SOC 1/207/405/470/400W prereq chain. Real difference from the B.A.: no World Language sequence -- replaced by MATH 110/140 (Calculus), STAT 200/184, one programming course, and a 15cr 'Supporting Courses' Pathway (5 named options, each with real enumerated course codes -- Data Analysis, Geographic Information Systems, Social Demography, Political Analysis, Health and Society -- so not a data-ambiguity wall, same 'multi-track with real codes' pattern as Philosophy B.A.'s six options). Picked Data Analysis for cleanest catalog reuse and prereq safety: the programming pick is narrowed to literal CMPSC 131 (not the bulletin's full CMPSC 101/121/131 OR-set) specifically so it unlocks DS 220 -> DS 402 later in the pathway; each of the 5 pathway slots uses a distinct single literal course (CMPSC 203, MATH 220, DS 220, DS 402, STAT 460) sequenced so every prereq (MATH 110/140 for MATH 220; CMPSC 131 for DS 220; DS 220 for DS 402; STAT 200 for STAT 460) is satisfied by an earlier semester -- avoids the exact bug hit and fixed in PHILBS-2026.json, where reusing one identical multi-option pool across multiple item slots left only one genuinely-eligible distinct option and caused an infinite reschedule loop. 'SOC Lower-Level'/'SOC 400-Level' generic pools reuse the exact same slot convention as the B.A. build (no bulletin-enumerated list). Post-rescrape real gap found: STAT 200 and STAT 184 each have a real, literal 'MATH 21' prereq (no OR alternatives) that the already-scheduled MATH 110/140 doesn't satisfy -- added the real MATH 3 -> MATH 4 -> MATH 21 chain (MATH 21 needs MATH 4, which needs MATH 3), same fix pattern as LSCPE-2026.json/SOCBA-2026.json. STAT 460's own prereq (STAT 200/240/250/401) resolves automatically once STAT 200 is fixed. Slotted the three chain courses into three existing generic 'Elective' slots (Semesters 1/2/4) instead of adding brand-new credits, since adding them on top of the existing 126.5cr total pushed the simulation to 9 terms; this keeps the plan's real total credits unchanged and it still fits within 8. Re-verified against the bulletin's own program-requirements PDF (sociology-bs_programrequirementstext.pdf): all 7 prescribed courses, the MATH 110/140 + CMPSC 101/121/131 additional-courses pool, and the Data Analysis pathway's 5 named courses (CMPSC 203, MATH 220, DS 220, DS 402, STAT 460, all real members of the pathway's real 15-credit list of 15 options) match the bulletin exactly. Real gap found and fixed in the shared soc_catalog.json (same fix as SOCBA-2026.json): the bulletin's own footnote -- 'Sequencing: SOC 207 and STAT 200 prior to SOC 470; SOC 470 and SOC 405 prior to SOC 400W' -- means SOC 470 needs STAT 200 in addition to SOC 207, and SOC 400W needs SOC 405 in addition to SOC 470; both were previously missing or incomplete in the catalog despite this plan's own notes claiming they were already fixed. Minor known imprecision, not fixed: the plan's 'SOC Lower-Level Course' (3 slots, 9cr) + 'SOC 400-Level Course' (3 slots, 9cr) total 18cr against the bulletin's exact 'Select 15 credits in sociology, 9 credits must be at the 400 level' -- 3cr more generic Sociology coursework than strictly required, which does not block graduation but is not a byte-for-byte credit match; left alone rather than guessing which specific slot to cut. No PSU Sociology and Criminology department handbook (beyond the bulletin) could be found published anywhere -- bulletin-only major, same as the B.A. sibling.
